_meta.indication: Long-term enzyme replacement therapy (ERT) for pediatric and adult patients with type 1 Gaucher disease

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Study I (Trial 032/TKT032), the single pivotal Phase 3 trial
pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, randomized, double-blind, parallel-dose-group (45 U/kg and 60 U/kg) study over 12 months
pivotal_trials.population: Treatment-naive patients age 4 years and older with Gaucher disease-related anemia and either thrombocytopenia or organomegaly; no disease-specific therapy for at least the previous 30 months
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoint was change from baseline in hemoglobin concentration in the 60 Unit/kg group at Month 12
pivotal_trials.result: Mean hemoglobin increase from baseline of 2.4 g/dL in the 60 U/kg group at Month 12 (p < 0.001); platelet count change +51 x10^9/L and spleen volume change -1.9 %BW

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Study II (Trial 039), active-controlled Phase 3 trial vs imiglucerase
pivotal_trials.design: 9-month, randomized, double-blind, active-controlled (imiglucerase), parallel-group, multinational study
pivotal_trials.population: Patients age 3 years and older with Gaucher disease-related anemia and either thrombocytopenia or organomegaly, not treated for at least the previous 12 months
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change from baseline in hemoglobin concentration at 9 months; treatment difference VPRIV minus imiglucerase
pivotal_trials.n: 34 patients randomized to VPRIV 60 U/kg (N=17) or imiglucerase 60 U/kg (N=17)
pivotal_trials.result: Mean hemoglobin increase from baseline of 1.6 g/dL with VPRIV at 9 months; mean treatment difference VPRIV minus imiglucerase 0.1 g/dL

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions were infusion-related reactions (51.9% of treatment-naive patients); other common reactions (>=10%) included headache (35.2%), upper respiratory tract infection (31.5%), pyrexia (22.2%) and dizziness (22.2%). The most serious adverse reactions were hypersensitivity reactions.
target_moa: Velaglucerase alfa is a recombinant human glucocerebrosidase (beta-glucocerebrosidase) that replaces the deficient lysosomal enzyme, catalyzing hydrolysis of glucocerebroside to glucose and ceramide and reducing its accumulation in macrophages in type 1 Gaucher disease.
modality: enzyme (recombinant human glucocerebrosidase glycoprotein produced by gene activation in a human fibroblast cell line)

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee meeting was held; the application states None, as the product was similar to other approved ERTs for type 1 Gaucher disease.

description.text: Added long-term efficacy data on hematological and organ volume parameters and bone mineral density data to labeling

citations.quote: This “Prior Approval” supplemental new drug application proposes the following changes: addition of long-term efficacy data on hematological and organ volume parameters and the inclusion of bone mineral density data.

orphan_indication.text: Velaglucerase alfa received orphan designation for the treatment of Type 1 Gaucher disease on June 8, 2009.

citations.quote: Velaglucerase alfa received orphan designation for the treatment of Type 1 Gaucher disease on June 8, 2009.

basis.text: The application received a priority review designation; the Phase 3 trials provided substantial evidence of efficacy.

citations.quote: This application received a priority review designation, and I agree with the clinical reviewers that the phase 3 trials submitted in support of this indication provide substantial evidence of efficacy.

summary.text: VPRIV was approved via the traditional (full) pathway for type 1 Gaucher disease; the application received orphan drug designation (June 8, 2009) and priority review, and no advisory committee was convened.

citations.quote: Velaglucerase alfa received orphan designation for the treatment of Type 1 Gaucher disease on June 8, 2009.
NDA 022575, submitted by Shire on August 31, 2009, and received on August 31, 2009, was filed and granted a priority review.
An Advisory Committee was not held due to the product's similarity to other approved enzyme replacement therapies for Type 1 Gaucher disease.

requirement.text: 1600-01: utilize an antibody screening cut point based on a mean + 1.645 standard deviation for assay values from treatment-naive Gaucher patients, applying the same methodology to the anti-imiglucerase ECL cut point.

citations.quote: 1600-01 Shire commits to utilize an antibody screening cut point based on a mean + 1.645 standard deviation for assay values from treatment naïve Gaucher patients. Shire will utilize the same methodology to calculate the anti-imiglucerase ECL cut point.

requirement.text: 1600-02: revise the cut point for the confirmatory anti-velaglucerase and anti-imiglucerase screening assays to a level less than or equal to the cut point of the screening assay.

citations.quote: 1600-02 Shire commits to revise the cut point for the confirmatory anti-velaglucerase and anti-imiglucerase screening assays to a level that is less than or equal to the cut point of the screening assay.

requirement.text: 1600-03: re-assess the IgE cut point for the current ECL methodology using a chemically synthesized hybrid control and support assay validation using patient baseline values.

citations.quote: 1600-03 Shire commits to re-assess the IgE cut point for the current ECL methodology using a chemically synthesized hybrid control. Shire commits to support assay validation using patient baseline values.

requirement.text: 1600-04: develop an assay to measure the ability of patient antibodies to block the uptake of velaglucerase and imiglucerase into target cells.

citations.quote: 1600-04 Shire commits to develop an assay to measure the ability of patient antibodies to block the uptake of velaglucerase and imiglucerase into target cells.

requirement.text: 1600-05: re-analyze all archived pharmacokinetic samples for Study TKT032 and recalculate velaglucerase alfa PK parameters.

citations.quote: 1600-05 Shire commits to re-analyze all archived pharmacokinetic (PK) samples for Study TKT032 (using adequate in-process quality controls and standard curves) and recalculate velaglucerase alfa PK parameters.

requirement.text: 1600-06: conduct a prospective PK study in patients with Type 1 Gaucher disease if the archived PK samples fail to adequately characterize velaglucerase alfa PK.

citations.quote: 1600-06 Shire commits to conduct a prospective PK study in patients with Type 1 Gaucher disease in the case that Shire fails to adequately characterize velaglucerase alfa PK using the archived PK samples (discussed under PMC #1600-05 above).

requirement.text: 1600-07: develop and implement a kinetic assay with a physiologically relevant substrate for drug substance and drug product release and stability testing.

citations.quote: 1600-07 Shire commits to develop and implement a kinetic assay with a physiologically relevant substrate for drug substance and drug product release and stability testing. Results and specifications will be included in the final report.

requirement.text: 1600-08: develop and implement a quantitative method that measures total carbohydrate content.

citations.quote: 1600-08 Shire commits to develop and implement a quantitative method that measures total carbohydrate content. Results and specifications will be included in the final report.

requirement.text: 1600-09: replace the non-quantitative SDS-PAGE Silver stain method with a quantitative SDS-PAGE Coomassie test.

citations.quote: 1600-09 Shire commits to replace the non-quantitative SDS-PAGE Silver stain method with a quantitative SDS-PAGE Coomassie test. Results and specifications will be included in the final report.
